The tube is bamboo, wood or animal bone, bamboo being the most common and cut from locally growing species. Bone usually comes from animals and is ground and polished into a smooth tube. For the wooden parts a dense local hardwood is usually chosen. The blowhole and fingerholes are carefully worked by hand, and the inside channel is smooth so that the air flows freely. Some well-made instruments are simply decorated or polished, keeping the original natural grain and texture.

Traditionally it is a courtship instrument, mostly played in private for the player's own pleasure, and it can also be joined to chanting, song and hula. A hula teacher can use the nose flute to produce a sound close to chanting, or blow and sing at once; Leilehua Yuen is one of the few contemporary Hawaiian musicians who plays this way.

The Hawaiian nose flute is an aerophone, Hornbostel–Sachs 421.111.22, of the nose-flute class. It is made from a single node of bamboo, with a nose blowhole and one to four fingerholes, and the player blows through a nostril and changes pitch by opening and closing the holes with the fingers. In Hawaii it is common in courtship and is also used for private amusement or with chanting, song and hula; a hula teacher can blow and sing at once, so that the flute sounds almost like recitation. Nose flutes in different regions need not be historically connected, being classed together mainly because the way of playing is similar.
夏威夷鼻笛音色獨特溫潤，帶有柔和的鼻腔共鳴特性，音質介於笛子與口哨之間。其音色較: The Hawaiian nose flute has a distinctive, warm timbre with a soft nasal resonance, its tone lying between a flute and a whistle. It is contained and quiet rather than bright and exciting like the transverse flute, with a warm, slightly nasal quality. The range is usually confined to the low middle and is limited in width, but the changes of pitch are fine and flexible. Because the air comes straight from the nasal cavity, the resonance happens mainly in the nose and mouth, which gives it its unusual resonance. Beside the carrying power of the traditional flute the nose flute sounds more intimate; beside the clarinet it lacks weight but has more of a raw, natural character. This sound suits meditative, still moods and is easily recognised in modern world music.
鼻笛各版本未必有歷史關聯，因相似吹奏方法而被歸類，見於波利尼西亞、環太平洋與非洲: The various versions of the nose flute need not be historically connected; they are classed together because the way of playing is similar, and they are found in Polynesia, around the Pacific rim and in Africa. In the Hawaiian Islands the ʻohe hano ihu is commonly a courtship instrument made from a single node of bamboo; old holdings in the Bishop Museum have a nose blowhole and two or three fingerholes, and oral accounts give one to four, placed according to the player's taste. It is played mainly in private, and can also accompany chanting, song and hula; a hula teacher can make the flute sound like chanting or play and sing at once, and Leilehua Yuen is one of the few contemporary musicians to play this way.
